spec.description: CPU, memory, storage and network across all hosts and per host.

spec.title: CPU
spec.description:
Non-idle share of all cores across all hosts, stacked by mode.
- Larger hosts weigh more
- `Other`: irq, softirq, nice and steal

spec.title: Memory used
spec.description:
`MemTotal - MemAvailable` summed across hosts, over their summed `MemTotal`.
- Page cache and reclaimable slab count as free
- Shifts when hosts join or leave

spec.title: Disk space used
spec.description:
Used share of all ext, XFS and ZFS filesystems, summed across hosts.
- As `df` computes it: root-reserved blocks count as neither used nor free
- Shifts when hosts join or leave

Values at the end of the dashboard range; hosts not reporting then are absent.
- Disk and network columns: the busiest device on the host
- `Uptime`: days
- `Disk Used%`: the fullest filesystem
- `TCP Estab.`: `CurrEstab`, which also counts `CLOSE_WAIT`
- `Health`: composite of CPU, memory and I/O; below 90 is worth a look

spec.title: CPU busy
spec.description:
Non-idle share of each host's cores.
- A row that ends before the right edge is a host that stopped reporting

spec.title: Memory used
spec.description: `1 - MemAvailable / MemTotal`: page cache and reclaimable slab count as free.

spec.title: I/O pressure
spec.description: Share of time at least one task waited on I/O, from PSI (`some`).

Hottest sensor per host, as a share of its own critical threshold.
- `Mean` close to `Peak`: the host runs hot all the time, not only under load
- 100 %: the critical point, where CPUs throttle; orange from 90 %
- Hosts without sensors, such as VMs, are not listed

Every ext, XFS, ZFS, NFS and CIFS mount, as of the end of the dashboard range.
- `Use trend`: each sparkline scales to its own row
- `Growth/day`: linear trend of free space over the last 7 days, whatever the dashboard range; a single large write or cleanup in that week skews it
- `State`: `rw` writable; `ro` read-only, as the kernel leaves a mount after disk errors; `error` when the mount does not answer, such as a lost network share
- NFS and CIFS mounts report the file server, shared with its other clients

spec.expr: max by (instance, mountpoint, fstype) ((node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"} - node_filesystem_free_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"}) / (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"} + node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"} - node_filesystem_free_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"}))

max by (instance, mountpoint, fstype) (-deriv(node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"}[7d])) * 86400 and on (instance, mountpoint) node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"}

max by (instance, mountpoint, fstype) ((node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"} - node_filesystem_free_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"}) / (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"} + node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"} - node_filesystem_free_bytes{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"}))

max by (instance, mountpoint, fstype) (node_filesystem_device_error{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"} * 2 or node_filesystem_readonly{job="integrations/unix",fstype=~"ext.*|xfs|zfs|nfs.*|cifs", mountpoint!~"/var/snap/.+"})

spec.title: Unclosed sockets
spec.description:
TCP sockets in the two closing states the kernel never times out while a process holds them.
- `FIN_WAIT2`: this host closed, the peer never did
- `CLOSE_WAIT`: the peer closed, the process never did, typically a program that does not close its connections
- Listed above 1000
- A steady climb that drops only when the owning process restarts

spec.expr: max by (instance, state) (max_over_time(node_tcp_connection_states{job="integrations/unix", state=~"fin_wait2|close_wait"}[$__interval])) and on (instance, state) (max by (instance, state) (max_over_time(node_tcp_connection_states{job="integrations/unix", state=~"fin_wait2|close_wait"}[$__range] @ end())) > 1000)

spec.title: TCP retransmits
spec.description:
Retransmitted TCP segments, as a share of all segments sent and per second.
- Listed above 1 %
- The share also moves with traffic: a steady retransmit rate reads higher when the host sends less

spec.expr: sum by (instance) (rate(node_netstat_Tcp_RetransSegs{job="integrations/unix"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (instance) (sum by (instance) (increase(node_netstat_Tcp_RetransSegs{job="integrations/unix"}[$__range] @ end())) / sum by (instance) (increase(node_netstat_Tcp_OutSegs{job="integrations/unix"}[$__range] @ end())) > 0.01)

sum by (instance) (rate(node_netstat_Tcp_RetransSegs{job="integrations/unix"}[$__range])) and on (instance) (sum by (instance) (increase(node_netstat_Tcp_RetransSegs{job="integrations/unix"}[$__range])) / sum by (instance) (increase(node_netstat_Tcp_OutSegs{job="integrations/unix"}[$__range])) > 0.01)

spec.title: Memory errors
spec.description:
Corrected and uncorrected ECC memory errors reported by the kernel EDAC driver.
- Corrected errors are an early sign of a failing memory module
- Hosts without an EDAC driver, such as VMs, never report any
- The host link opens its kernel log filtered to `EDAC`

spec.expr: sum by (instance) (increase(node_edac_correctable_errors_total{job="integrations/unix"}[$__interval])) + sum by (instance) (increase(node_edac_uncorrectable_errors_total{job="integrations/unix"}[$__interval])) and on (instance) (round(sum by (instance) (increase(node_edac_correctable_errors_total{job="integrations/unix"}[$__range] @ end())) + sum by (instance) (increase(node_edac_uncorrectable_errors_total{job="integrations/unix"}[$__range] @ end()))) > 0)

value.title: Kernel EDAC messages for this host

spec.title: Links
spec.description:
Link state changes and frame errors of Ethernet interfaces, virtual ones included.
- `Link changes`: a drop and its recovery count as two; a bond member that drops leaves the host online on the remaining members
- `Frame errors`: frames received or sent damaged, typically a faulty cable, transceiver or port

spec.expr: label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (instance) (increase(node_network_carrier_changes_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__range]))) > 0, "event", "Link changes", "", ""), "tab", "Interfaces", "", "") or label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (instance) (increase(node_network_receive_errs_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__range]) + increase(node_network_transmit_errs_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__range]))) > 0, "event", "Frame errors", "", ""), "tab", "Traffic", "", "")

label_replace(label_replace(sum by (instance) (increase(node_network_carrier_changes_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__interval])), "event", "Link changes", "", ""), "tab", "Interfaces", "", "") and on (instance) (round(sum by (instance) (increase(node_network_carrier_changes_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__range] @ end()))) > 0) or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (instance) (increase(node_network_receive_errs_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__interval]) + increase(node_network_transmit_errs_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__interval])), "event", "Frame errors", "", ""), "tab", "Traffic", "", "") and on (instance) (round(sum by (instance) (increase(node_network_receive_errs_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__range] @ end()) + increase(node_network_transmit_errs_total{job="integrations/unix", device=~"en.*|eth.*"}[$__range] @ end()))) > 0)

spec.title: Conntrack
spec.description:
Fill of the kernel connection tracking table, as a share of its limit.
- Listed from 50 %
- At 100 % the kernel drops new connections

spec.expr: max by (instance) (max_over_time((node_nf_conntrack_entries{job="integrations/unix"} / node_nf_conntrack_entries_limit{job="integrations/unix"})[$__interval:])) and on (instance) (max by (instance) (max_over_time((node_nf_conntrack_entries{job="integrations/unix"} / node_nf_conntrack_entries_limit{job="integrations/unix"})[$__range:] @ end())) >= 0.5)

spec.title: OOM kills
spec.description:
Processes the kernel killed for lack of memory.
- The host link opens the OOM kills dashboard with the victims

spec.expr: sum by (instance) (increase(node_vmstat_oom_kill{job="integrations/unix"}[$__interval])) and on (instance) (round(sum by (instance) (increase(node_vmstat_oom_kill{job="integrations/unix"}[$__range] @ end()))) > 0)

spec.title: Clock
spec.description:
Hosts whose clock drifted or lost sync.
- Out of sync: offset above 50 ms and not shrinking, or the kernel reporting no sync with a maximum error of 16 s
- `Out of sync`: total time in that state; listed from 10 minutes
- `Offset`: the largest offset in the range

spec.expr: max by (instance) (max_over_time(abs(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"})[$__range:])) and on (instance) (count_over_time((count by (instance) ((node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} > 0.05 and deriv(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"}[5m]) >= 0) or (node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} < -0.05 and deriv(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"}[5m]) <= 0) or (node_timex_sync_status{job="integrations/unix"} == 0 and node_timex_maxerror_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} >= 16)))[$__range:1m]) * 60 >= 600)

count_over_time((count by (instance) ((node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} > 0.05 and deriv(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"}[5m]) >= 0) or (node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} < -0.05 and deriv(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"}[5m]) <= 0) or (node_timex_sync_status{job="integrations/unix"} == 0 and node_timex_maxerror_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} >= 16)))[$__range:1m]) * 60 and on (instance) (count_over_time((count by (instance) ((node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} > 0.05 and deriv(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"}[5m]) >= 0) or (node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} < -0.05 and deriv(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"}[5m]) <= 0) or (node_timex_sync_status{job="integrations/unix"} == 0 and node_timex_maxerror_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} >= 16)))[$__range:1m]) * 60 >= 600)

max by (instance) (max_over_time(abs(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"})[$__interval:])) and on (instance) (count_over_time((count by (instance) ((node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} > 0.05 and deriv(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"}[5m]) >= 0) or (node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} < -0.05 and deriv(node_timex_offset_seconds{job="integrations/unix"}[5m]) <= 0) or (node_timex_sync_status{job="integrations/unix"} == 0 and node_timex_maxerror_seconds{job="integrations/unix"} >= 16)))[$__range:1m] @ end()) * 60 >= 600)

spec.description:
One row per host reporting at the end of the dashboard range.
- `Uptime`: days
- `Storage`: every ext, XFS and ZFS filesystem, each device counted once

spec.title: Network
spec.description:
Summed over physical NICs: `en*`, `eth*`; received up, sent down.
- Bond and tunnel traffic counts once, on the NIC beneath

spec.title: Load and pressure
spec.description:
Saturation, averaged across hosts.
- `CPU`, `Memory`, `I/O`: share of time at least one task stalled on the resource, from PSI (`some`)
- `Load per core`, dashed: summed 5 m load average over the total core count; 100 % means as many runnable or I/O-blocked tasks as cores

spec.title: Disk I/O
spec.description:
Summed over physical disks: `sd*`, `vd*`, `nvme*n*`; read up, write down.
- RAID, LVM and multipath I/O counts once, on the disks beneath

spec.title: CPU
spec.description:
Stacked to 100 % of all cores.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: System - Processes executing in kernel mode
User - Normal processes executing in user mode
Nice - Niced processes executing in user mode
Iowait - Waiting for I/O to complete
Steal - Time spent in other operating systems when running in a virtualized environment
Idle - Waiting for something to happen

spec.expr: sum by(instance) (rate(node_cpu_guest_seconds_total{instance="$hostname"}[$__rate_interval])) / on(instance) group_left sum by (instance)((rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{instance="$hostname"}[$__rate_interval]))) > 0

matcher.options: Idle - Waiting for something to happen
Iowait - Waiting for I/O to complete
Nice - Niced processes executing in user mode
Steal - Time spent in other operating systems when running in a virtualized environment
System - Processes executing in kernel mode
User - Normal processes executing in user mode

spec.title: System Load per Core
spec.description:
Load averages divided by the core count.
- 100 %: as many runnable or I/O-blocked tasks as cores; above it, tasks wait
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Context Switches / Interrupts
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.title: RAM Used
spec.description:
`1 - MemAvailable / MemTotal`: page cache and reclaimable slab count as free.
- At the end of the dashboard range

spec.title: CPU Busy
spec.description:
Non-idle share averaged across all cores.
- At the end of the dashboard range
- One saturated core on a many-core host barely moves it

spec.title: SWAP Used
spec.description:
At the end of the dashboard range.
- Reads 0 % on hosts without swap

spec.title: Memory Pages Swap In / Out
spec.description:
Sustained swap-out: memory pressure.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Memory
spec.description:
Physical memory stacked to `MemTotal`; swap in use stacks on top.
- `Apps`: what remains after the other categories
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: Apps - Memory used by user-space applications
PageTables - Memory used to map between virtual and physical memory addresses
SwapCache - Memory that keeps track of pages that have been fetched from swap but not yet been modified
Slab - Memory used by the kernel to cache data structures for its own use (caches like inode, dentry, etc)
Cache - Parked file data (file content) cache
Hardware Corrupted - Amount of RAM that the kernel identified as corrupted / not working

spec.title: File Descriptor
spec.description:
File handles allocated system-wide.
- The limit appears only in the legend
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Instantaneous Queue Size
spec.description:
Requests in flight at the moment of each scrape, unlike the averaged queue size.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Average Queue Size
spec.description:
Time-weighted mean of requests in flight.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Disk Average Wait Time
spec.description:
Per request, time in the queue plus time being served.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: File Nodes Free
spec.description:
Running out of inodes stops file creation even with free space.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Disk Throughput
spec.description:
Physical disks only; LVM, RAID and loop devices count on the disks beneath.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Filesystem Space Available
spec.description:
Space available to unprivileged users: root-reserved blocks excluded.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: ICMP Errors
spec.description: Messages received with a bad checksum, length or header.

spec.title: UDP In / Out
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.title: Network Traffic by Packets
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.title: NF Conntrack
spec.description:
Connections tracked by netfilter.
- At the limit, new connections are dropped
- The limit appears only in the legend
- `Not tracked`: connection tracking is not loaded in the kernel, as on hosts without Docker or NAT

spec.title: Processes Status
spec.description:
`Blocked`: uninterruptible sleep, usually waiting on disk I/O.
- `Hung Tasks`: blocked past the kernel's hung-task timeout
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Sockstat TCP
spec.description:
`Orphaned`: closed by the application, still held by the kernel.
- `TIME_WAIT`: closed, waiting out late packets
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Memory Vmalloc
spec.description:
Kernel virtual allocations, mostly by modules and drivers.
- The limit appears only in the legend
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: Vmalloc Free Chunk – Largest available block in vmalloc area
Vmalloc Total – Total size of the vmalloc memory area
Vmalloc Used – Portion of vmalloc area currently in use

spec.title: CPU Basic
spec.description:
Stacked to 100 % of all cores.
- `Busy Other`: nice and steal

spec.title: Memory Basic
spec.description:
Physical memory stacked to `Total`; swap in use stacks on top.
- `Used`: what remains after the other categories
- `Cache + Buffer`: page cache, buffers and reclaimable slab

spec.title: TCP Direct Transition
spec.description:
New TCP connections per second, by which side opened them.
- `Active`: connections this host initiated
- `Passive`: connections it accepted
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Network Traffic
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.title: TCP Connections
spec.description: `CurrEstab`, which also counts `CLOSE_WAIT`.

spec.title: TCP Errors
spec.description:
`Listen Overflows`, `Listen Drops`: connections refused because an accept queue was full.
- `SYN Cookies Sent`: the SYN queue overflowed
- `Out-of-order Queued`: segments arriving ahead of a gap
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: UDP Errors
spec.description:
`No Listener`: datagrams sent to a closed port.
- `Buffer Errors`: a socket buffer was full
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: ICMP In / Out
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.title: Sockstat UDP
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.title: Sockstat Used
spec.description: Every protocol, UNIX sockets included.

spec.title: Disk I/O Utilization
spec.description:
Share of time the device had I/O in flight.
- SSDs and arrays serve requests in parallel, so 100 % is not saturation there
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Memory Anonymous
spec.description:
Memory not backed by files: heap, stacks and anonymous mappings.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Memory Writeback and Dirty
spec.description:
High dirty or writeback memory: disk writes falling behind.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: Writeback – Memory currently being flushed to disk
Dirty – Memory marked dirty (pending write to disk)
NFS Unstable – Pages sent to NFS server, awaiting storage commit

spec.title: Memory Slab
spec.description:
Kernel object caches; reclaimable slab is freed under memory pressure.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: SReclaimable – Potentially reclaimable slab memory (e.g., inode cache)

spec.title: Disk R/W Merged
spec.description:
Adjacent requests the block layer combined before issuing them.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Memory Committed
spec.description:
Address space promised to processes, against the commit limit.
- Linux overcommits by default, so `Committed_AS` above the limit is allowed; it raises the risk of OOM kills under load
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: Committed_AS – Memory promised to processes (not necessarily used)

spec.title: Memory LRU Active / Inactive (%)
spec.description:
Share of RAM on the kernel's LRU lists; reclaim takes inactive pages first.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: Inactive – Less recently used memory, more likely to be reclaimed
Active – Recently used memory, retained unless under pressure

spec.title: Memory Unevictable and MLocked
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.title: Memory Shared and Mapped
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.legendFormat: Mapped – Memory mapped from files (e.g., libraries, mmap)
Shmem – Shared memory used by processes and tmpfs
ShmemHugePages – Shared memory (shmem/tmpfs) allocated with HugePages
PMD Mapped – Shmem/tmpfs backed by Transparent HugePages (PMD)

spec.title: Memory HugePages
spec.description:
Page counts multiplied by the huge page size.
- `Reserved`: promised to a mapping, not yet faulted in
- `Surplus`: allocated above the configured pool

spec.title: Network Traffic Errors
spec.description:
Errors per bucket reported by the NIC and its driver; only nonzero buckets are drawn.
- Usually cabling, a failing port or a driver fault

spec.title: Network Traffic Drop
spec.description:
Receive drops: full buffers or driver limits; transmit drops: congestion or full queues.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Network Traffic Multicast
spec.description:
mDNS, SSDP and cluster protocols use multicast.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Disk Space Used Basic
spec.description: As `df` computes it: root-reserved blocks count as neither used nor free.

spec.title: Root FS Used
spec.description:
As `df` computes it: root-reserved blocks count as neither used nor free.
- At the end of the dashboard range

spec.expr: (node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$hostname", mountpoint="/", fstype!="rootfs"} - node_filesystem_free_bytes{instance="$hostname", mountpoint="/", fstype!="rootfs"}) * 100 / (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$hostname", mountpoint="/", fstype!="rootfs"} + node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$hostname", mountpoint="/", fstype!="rootfs"} - node_filesystem_free_bytes{instance="$hostname", mountpoint="/", fstype!="rootfs"})

spec.title: Sys Load
spec.description:
1-minute load average divided by the core count.
- At the end of the dashboard range
- 100 %: as many runnable or I/O-blocked tasks as cores

spec.title: Filesystem Used
spec.description:
`size - avail`, so root-reserved blocks count as used.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Hardware Temperature Monitor
spec.description:
Hottest `hwmon` sensor per chip; dashed: the chip's lowest critical threshold.
- CPU, NIC and board sensors where the hardware exposes them
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Memory Kernel / CPU
spec.description:
Small in normal operation; growth tracks thread count and loaded modules.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: PerCPU – Dynamically allocated per-CPU memory (used by kernel modules)

spec.title: Time Synchronized Status
spec.description:
`Sync status`: 1 while the kernel considers the clock synchronised.
- `Frequency Adjustment`: rate correction applied to the clock

spec.title: Memory Page Faults
spec.description:
Major faults read from disk; minor faults are served from memory.
- Sustained major faults: memory pressure
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.legendFormat: Pgfault - Page major and minor fault ops

matcher.options: Pgfault - Page major and minor fault ops

spec.title: Memory Pages In / Out
spec.description:
All block I/O through the page cache, swap included.
- `pgpgin` and `pgpgout` count KiB, not pages
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

Every ext, XFS, ZFS, NFS and CIFS mount on the host, as of the end of the dashboard range.
- `Size`, `Avail` and `Use%` as `df` computes them
- `Inode%`: share of file entries used; when full, no new file can be created whatever the free space
- `State`: `ro` read-only, as the kernel leaves a mount after disk errors; `error` when the mount does not answer, such as a lost network share
- NFS and CIFS mounts report the file server, shared with its other clients

spec.title: Memory LRU Active / Inactive Detail
spec.description:
LRU lists split by page type; reclaim takes inactive pages first.
- `anon`: process memory such as heap, stacks and tmpfs
- `file`: page cache and memory-mapped files
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: File Nodes Used
spec.description:
Running out of inodes stops file creation even with free space.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Sockstat Memory Size
spec.description:
Kernel buffer memory held by sockets.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Netstat IP In / Out Octets
spec.description:
All IP traffic, every protocol.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Disk IOps
spec.description:
Physical disks only; LVM, RAID and loop devices count on the disks beneath.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: ARP Entries
spec.description:
Table growth: scanning or a misconfigured network.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Time Synchronized Drift
spec.description:
Clock offset from the NTP reference, and the kernel's error bounds.
- Errors on the right axis: the maximum error climbs to seconds between syncs

spec.title: Interfaces
spec.description:
Every interface except loopback, as of the end of the dashboard range.
- `down`: enabled but without a link
- `disabled`: switched off administratively

spec.expr: max by (device, operstate, duplex, address) (label_replace(node_network_info{instance="$hostname", device!="lo", adminstate="down"}, "operstate", "disabled", "", "") or node_network_info{instance="$hostname", device!="lo", adminstate!="down"})

spec.title: Softnet Packets
spec.description:
Packets the kernel's receive path handled.
- `Busiest`: the highest single-core value at each point; well above the average, one core is pinned
- Drops: the per-CPU backlog was full
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Time PLL Adjust
spec.description:
NTP phase-locked loop time constant.
- Lower: faster correction, less stability

spec.title: Systemd Sockets Accepted
spec.description:
Connections accepted per systemd socket unit.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Systemd Units State
spec.description: Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden.

spec.title: TCP In / Out
spec.description:
Segments, data and control.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Cooling Device Utilization
spec.description:
Throttling relative to each device type's maximum state; only nonzero values are drawn.
- `Processor`, `intel_powerclamp`, `TCC Offset`: CPU throttling, not fans
- PCIe link-speed devices are left out

spec.title: CPU Saturation
spec.description:
Share of CPU demand spent waiting to run: `waiting / (running + waiting)`.
- `Busiest core`: the core with the most waiting time at each point; well above `All cores`, one core is pinned
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: CPU Schedule Timeslices
spec.description:
Tasks the scheduler ran per second, a proxy for task switching per core.
- `Busiest`: the highest single-core value at each point; well above the average, one core is pinned
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: OOM Killer
spec.description:
Kills per bucket.
- The panel link opens OOM Kills, which names the victims

spec.title: Network Operational Status
spec.description:
One bar per interface: `Up` while it has a link.
- Interfaces switched off administratively are left out

spec.expr: max by (device) (node_network_up{instance="$hostname", device!="lo"}) and on (device) node_network_info{instance="$hostname", adminstate="up"}

spec.title: Softnet Out of Quota
spec.description:
Times the receive path ran out of budget with packets still queued.
- `Busiest`: the highest single-core value at each point; well above the average, one core is pinned
- Frequent squeezes: too little CPU for packet processing

spec.title: PIDs Number and Limit
spec.description:
The limit appears only in the legend.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Threads Number and Limit
spec.description:
The limit appears only in the legend.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Processes Detailed States
spec.description:
Stacked by state; zombie and stopped processes show in the legend.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: TCP Connection States
spec.description:
Every state but `established` and `listen`; a state with no sockets reads 0.
- `established` is in Host / TCP · TCP Connections
- `close_wait` growing: an application is not closing sockets its peer closed
- `fin_wait2` growing: this host closed its side, the peer never closed its own
- `syn_recv` spiking: handshakes arriving faster than accepted

spec.title: CPU Frequency Scaling
spec.description:
Current frequency of the fastest, average and slowest core, against the allowed range.
- Empty on hosts without CPU frequency scaling, such as most VMs
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Pressure Stall Information
spec.description:
Share of time tasks stalled on the resource, from PSI; `Some` down, `Full` up.
- `Some`: at least one task stalled
- `Full`: every non-idle task stalled at once
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden
- Kernel documentation: https://docs.kernel.org/accounting/psi.html

spec.title: Pressure
spec.description:
Share of time at least one task waited on the resource, from PSI (`some`).
- At the end of the dashboard range

spec.title: UDP Queue
spec.description:
Memory held by queued UDP datagrams, IPv4 and IPv6 summed.
- `RX`: waiting to be read by the application
- `TX`: waiting to be sent

spec.title: Network Saturation
spec.description:
Throughput as a share of the reported link speed.
- Interfaces with no reported speed, such as loopback, are left out
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Sockstat Average Socket Memory
spec.description:
Socket buffer memory divided by sockets in use.
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: TCP Socket Queue
spec.description:
Bytes queued in TCP sockets.
- `RX`: received, unread by the application
- `TX`: sent, unacknowledged by the peer, plus each listening socket's backlog limit as a constant floor
- Series that stayed at zero over the range are hidden

spec.title: Hosts
